title: 'Red Scare': Columbia Student Formerly Detained by ICE Describes 'Chilling Effect' on Campus
author: Mehdi Hasan
content:
Columbia University is back in the spotlight, after the university once again
[failed](https://www.columbiaspectator.com/news/2026/02/26/dhs-agents-detain-
columbia-student-after-entering-university-owned-residence-shipman-reports/)
to protect another one of its students from being unlawfully detained by ICE,
this time international student from Azerbaijan, Ellie Aghayeva.

Though the student was quickly
[released](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/02/26/nyregion/columbia-university-
ice-student.html) after a meeting at the White House between President Donald
Trump and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, the question still remains - can
international students trust Columbia University? Can they protest without
fear?

In this 'Mehdi Unfiltered' interview, **Mohsen Mahdawi** - a Columbia student
who was infamously [detained](https://zeteo.com/p/ice-ambushed-mohsen-mahdawi-
in-a) by ICE last year at his citizenship interview - describes to **Mehdi**
the **" chilling effect"** taking place on campus, after the arrest of him and
other pro-Palestine students, and the university's $221 million
[settlement](https://www.npr.org/2025/07/25/nx-s1-5479240/columbia-trump-
administration-settlement-details) with the Trump administration.

**" If this is not a red scare, and if it's not a McCarthy era, and if it's
not authoritarianism, what else would it be?" **Mahdawi says to Mehdi.

[Subscribe now](https://zeteo.com/subscribe)

Mahdawi tells Mehdi that some of his fellow students are now afraid to, **"
write academic papers that reflect their own beliefs and opinion** _**"**_
because they fear Columbia may share that information with the Trump
administration. He also explains why many pro-Palestine students are now
taking their activism off the campus.

Mehdi also asks Mahdawi about his family in the occupied West Bank, with
Mahdawi sharing that four of his cousins have been** "murdered [in] cold blood
since October 7th."**

**Paid subscribers** can watch the full interview to hear Mahdawi discuss the
latest updates on his deportation case, and what he makes of the Trump
administration's embrace of Israeli settlers in the West Bank.
